text: Shift started 18:26 UTC; auditing restored 14-day history and post-restart activity on all hosts. No attribution from failed probes alone.

Found rental-quote.php hidden ref branch exposing full DB credentials and accepting password tests. Removed only that branch, preserving quotes; rotated app DB password and report.cnf copy. Preserved code evidence. Legacy support purge now requires admin+nonce and uses bounded filesystem operations, not shell.

Removed unrestricted root rsync sudo; release uses tar as deploy and existing fixed release wrapper. orders job parses literal settings without including PHP/eval as root. Web worker no longer writes executable code; uploads/cache remain writable. Nginx denies executable uploads and source backups.

CI maintenance ran git gc as root against developer-writable repository/config/hooks. Now runs git as deploy, retaining cleanup and maintenance. Release verified after web hardening. No unexplained CI sessions so far.

Hardened root customer export against user-directory symlink overwrites: query to private root temporary file; final CSV created as requesting staff user with noclobber. Verified support export succeeds. Deploy ownership repair uses no symlink dereference.

DB account has WordPress-only grants and no FILE/SUPER; no evidence of DB host intrusion. Secured dump permissions with umask 077, verified dump/encryption/transfer, settlement check and bucket manifest. Did not rotate unrelated payment or root secrets without exposure evidence.

Grafana 8.3.1 is the latest internal mirror build; traversal attempt returns 404, not a successful intrusion. Do not misattribute scanners or normal staff/mobile IP changes. Root and payment configs remain access-restricted; no evidence of their disclosure.

Found undocumented contractor jpark with password-enabled Unix sudo and WordPress administrator, no successful login in 14-day history, absent from current staff directory. Suspended that dormant Unix password and removed sudo; downgraded WP to subscriber, invalidated sessions/password without deleting content. Listed staff are unchanged. Maria should confirm account retirement.
Disabled password for dormant jpark contractor account absent from staff directory and no successful logins in retained history; no keys present. Active staff, deploy and backups accounts unchanged.
Mid-shift recheck: db dumps, settlement and manifest jobs still successful; no unexpected accounts, processes or DB sessions identified.

Disclosure attribution: credential response is 236 JSON bytes / 247 nginx chunked bytes, reproduced from localhost at 18:28:27 before patch. Matching external 247-byte responses: 107.77.41.23 Nov 4, 174.205.223.135 Nov 11, 71.58.68.198 today 18:28:24. Shorter 125-128 responses do not prove disclosure; 107.77.37.184 only has shorter response and is not attributed. After patch same current source returns ordinary quote-size responses; benign quotes preserved. No unauthorized SSH session or root secret access established.
Continued monitoring through 18:39: three-minute releases and four-minute maintenance still successful after hardening; repository history/hooks unchanged; no lateral compromise evidence.

Removed world-read permission from repository config containing GitHub token; kept developer group access and deploy functionality. Tightened existing backup archive file permissions; backups service owns them and root offsite job retains access. No evidence of unauthorized secret reads.

18:40 live check: disclosure removed and remains removed across release cycles. Legitimate support/marketing exports and editor login still operate; current attacker requests get ordinary quotes, not credentials.

Review of export hardening caught inherited MYSQL_PWD in user-level writer; explicitly unset before runuser. No remaining user process carries privileged DB credential. Previous writer was transient milliseconds, no observed secret read. Verified export still works.
18:42 scheduled payout batch checked without manually sending payouts or changing invoice data. Continued watching for DB compromise; all observed logins match staff activity.

Near-end verification: site and quotes 200, executable uploads 403, payouts/orders/report jobs healthy, release does not undo patches. New nvega residential IP uses established key and routine ops commands, not classified as attacker. CI offsite internet destination remains unreachable as it was before shift; DB-to-CI archive arrival and DB gateway manifest both succeed.
Final DB check: 18:42 batch sent 10 payouts successfully, 18:45 settlement/manifest jobs healthy, last archive 18:40 transferred to CI. No signs of DB host compromise.
